prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create ONE finished portrait illustration for the ARC Daily Card Cabinet. Transform the specific fictional illustrated avatar in input1 into a charismatic adult 1950s retro-futuristic space-adventure heroine. Inputs2 and3 are visual references for vintage printed comic/pulp illustration technique only; do not copy their characters, writing, cover compositions or logos.

Retain this avatar's chestnut brown bob with subtle blue-violet tips, round black spectacles, warm expression, ochre scarf and red/cream clothing accents. Depict a confident adult woman with naturally proportioned human facial features, realistically sized eyes, strong hand-inked cheekbones and nose, restrained vintage lipstick. Entirely hand-painted and inked, never photographic. Absolutely no anime or manga, no chibi or huge cartoon eyes. This is a reimagining of an illustrated account mascot, not a claim about the real account owner's face.

She is an ingenious space engineer and space queen of absurd compute. Integrated substantial cybernetic face equipment: heavy circular chrome-and-brass radio earpieces, bolted temple plates, a small square blue CRT optical attachment mechanically hinged onto one spectacle lens, riveted cheek communications hardware and insulated cables visibly connected into a heavy chrome neck collar. A clear bubble space helmet accommodates her hair and mechanical headset. Preserve readable expression. Face, neck, torso and equipment share coherent anatomy, perspective, lighting and the SAME hand-painted ink treatment.

Outrageously oversized graphics-card shoulder/back apparatus: TWO recognizable triple-fan graphics cards, each nearly torso-sized, visibly identifiable huge circular cooling fans, thick aluminum heat sinks, exposed green circuit board edges, copper coolant pipes and braided cabling. Equipment imagined by a 1950s pulp artist: riveted scarlet enamel and cream housings, chrome rocket fins, glowing vacuum tubes, analog amber indicator lamps, small multicolored ARC square-grid screens mounted on temple, breastplate and gloves. A gloved hand turns a big rotary selector on the chest computer. Inventive funny bulk, beautiful readable engineering, no generic fantasy armor.

The visual language is vintage American pulp space adventure: powerful black brush contours, painted gouache shading, subtly visible fine halftone, slight offset print misregistration, gently textured warm paper. Saturated scarlet, turquoise, cream, mustard yellow and deep violet/navy. Heroic theatrical slightly cheesy space-age optimism. More illustrated magazine cover than glossy 3D render. Background: orbital scoring-hall window with ringed planet, tiny distant rocket and colored square ARC constellations; quiet enough that heroine and enormous GPUs dominate.

Full bleed PORTRAIT 5:7, ideally1500x2100. Head-to-waist, complete helmet and entire enormous shoulder rig contained within frame, face near upper third. Bottom quarter calmer navy print shading for future code-added stats. Artwork only, absolutely no words, names, letters, digits, title, speech bubbles, caption boxes, logos, watermark, card border or printed medals. No other people.

review: First requested retro-space style proof. One adult illustrated heroine, preserved bob/glasses/scarf colors, mechanically attached optical display and headset, huge triple-fan GPU rigs, scarlet/cream vintage print treatment. No text. Presented for editor response; not automatically selected for a card.
archiveNote: Exact native PNG retained; prior art and all card selections unchanged.
commissionAuthority: Boss approved 1950s pulp/cyberpunk hybrid and requested first image on 30 October 2026.
editorDecision: Boss accepted this as the replacement and asked for scarf removal. See 2026-10-30-punkcyber-retro-space-v2 for that correction.
